extracted.intended_audience: public relations professionals and PR agencies pitching exclusive stories to top-tier media
extracted.subtask_description: Tactical guidance for PR practitioners on selecting Tier 1 outlets and pitching/negotiating exclusive story placements, then managing publication and measuring outcomes. Covers pitch construction, agreement terms, process management, and relationship-building.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding exclusives vs. embargoes
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish between an exclusive (one outlet gets sole rights to break a story first) and an embargo (multiple outlets may publish simultaneously at an agreed time).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclusives can generate greater impact (Cision research: exclusive stories receive 42% more social engagement) but require strict agreements about timing and access. Embargoes are better for major announcements where broad, simultaneous coverage is desired. Choose the right approach based on your goals and the news value of the announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tier 1 media characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize Tier 1 outlets as major national newspapers, broadcast networks, and leading industry publications with the largest reach and highest credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These outlets maintain strict editorial standards and receive hundreds of pitches daily; expect intense competition (average journalist receives 100+ pitches weekly; Tier 1 often exceeds 300). Use this to set expectations and ensure your story has genuine news value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the outlet’s readership matches your target demographic before offering an exclusive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review outlet media kits for detailed audience data and match topics (e.g., B2B software → TechCrunch rather than Entertainment Weekly). If the audience doesn't align, the exclusive is unlikely to perform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial focus fit
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirm your story aligns with the outlet’s beat and the specific reporter’s coverage area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study recent coverage to verify fit (example: The Wall Street Journal’s enterprise tech reporter likely won’t cover consumer gadget launches). Pitching outside an outlet’s editorial focus reduces chances of placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitive landscape research
rubrics_metrics.description: Research whether the outlet has covered similar stories or competitors recently to gauge interest and avoid conflicts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This helps you understand timing, angle opportunities, and whether the outlet will see your story as fresh or redundant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject line strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Craft a subject line that signals exclusivity and a compelling hook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead with “EXCLUSIVE:” followed by a concise news hook (example: “EXCLUSIVE: First AI-Powered Ocean Cleanup System Launches”). Journalists spend 3–5 seconds scanning emails, so the subject line must communicate urgency and newsworthiness immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opening paragraph clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: State immediately that you’re offering an exclusive and include any time constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: “I’m offering you exclusive first access to cover [Company X’s] breakthrough technology, with a 48-hour window for response.” Be explicit about exclusivity and deadlines to avoid confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value proposition in the pitch
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly articulate why the story matters to the outlet’s audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include key statistics, market impact, and broader industry implications to show relevance and news value. Explain the audience benefit, not just the client’s.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting materials availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer comprehensive resources to enable reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List what you can provide: executive interviews, customer testimonials, product demos, data insights, visuals. Demonstrating you can deliver these materials increases the outlet’s willingness to accept an exclusive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structuring mutually beneficial agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Define clear terms for the exclusive that serve both PR and journalist needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key elements include: duration of exclusivity, access to sources and materials, publication timing windows, distribution rights after the exclusive period, social media coordination, and quote approval processes. Document these terms in writing (even informally via email) to prevent misunderstandings and protect both parties’ interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document terms in writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure agreement terms are recorded to avoid disputes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even informal email confirmation is recommended. Documenting duration, access, timing, distribution rights, social coordination, and approval processes prevents misunderstandings and enforces mutual expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-publication management
rubrics_metrics.description: Manage tasks between acceptance and publication to ensure a smooth run-up to the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedule interviews promptly, deliver supporting materials on time, respond quickly to fact-checking requests, review quotes accurately but avoid excessive editing, and confirm publication timing with the journalist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication day management
rubrics_metrics.description: Actions to take on the day the story goes live.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor for the story going live, share on social media only after the outlet posts, thank the journalist, and track immediate coverage and engagement metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-exclusive follow-up
rubrics_metrics.description: Activities after the exclusive window closes to maximize impact and learn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin broader media outreach, share coverage with stakeholders, document lessons learned, and maintain the relationship with the journalist for future opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Building long-term media relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: Invest in ongoing, trust-based relationships with journalists to increase future exclusive opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow journalists’ work, engage thoughtfully on social media, provide useful background information, respect deadlines and preferences, and consistently deliver on promises. (Cision 2024: 82% of journalists prefer working with PR contacts they know.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Measuring success — quantitative metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Track numerical indicators to evaluate the exclusive placement’s reach and business impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantitative metrics include article reach and readership, social media engagement, website traffic from coverage, lead generation or conversion impact, and syndication pickup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measuring success — qualitative metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess non-numeric outcomes that reflect message and brand impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Qualitative metrics include message accuracy, spokesperson quote placement, visual asset usage, competitor mention context, and overall story sentiment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common pitfalls to avoid
rubrics_metrics.description: Frequent mistakes that undermine exclusive pitches and their execution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid offering the same story to multiple outlets, missing agreed-upon deadlines, over-controlling the editorial process, providing insufficient supporting materials, and neglecting clear agreement terms.
